provider_query: Hacker News discussion of Dan McKinley's essay Choose Boring Technology, quote one reader comment
answer:
Dan McKinley’s 2015 essay [Choose Boring Technology](https://mcfunley.com/choose-boring-technology) (also at [boringtechnology.club](https://boringtechnology.club/)) argues that teams have only a few “innovation tokens,” so most of the stack should be well-understood tools whose failure modes are known.

### One reader comment (HN, June 7, 2020)

From **nine_k** on the large 2020 thread ([item 23444594](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=23444594)):

> I still think that "boring" is a wrong word. Choose the technology you know in and out, and are immediately productive with. Choose the technology which is sure to be around in 5-7 years, preferably 10-15. Choose the technology for which you are comfortable hiring the next 15 engineers. This does not mean that you need to choose something unpleasant, unergonomic, or ancient. Neither does it mean that you need to choose exclusively among the top 5 most used in the field. The key thing here is to *avoid surprises*, unknown unknowns. You won't have the time to learn from a novice level while building a new company. A number of wildly successful MVPs were implemented with obscure (or then-obscure) technology which authors knew very well… ViaWeb was written in Lisp. YouTube was (and still largely is) written in Python… The initial Rust compiler was written in OCaml.

### Up to 8 relevant HN threads

1. **[Choose Boring Technology (2015)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=23444594)** — June 7, 2020; **459 points, 282 comments**. Main long discussion; source of the quote above.  
2. **[Choose Boring Technology (2015)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=30389591)** — Feb 18, 2022; **42 points, 13 comments**. Readers reframe “boring” as “tried and true” and note that Node had become practical by 2022.  
3. **[Choose Boring Technology](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=25322651)** — Dec 6, 2020; **205 points, 204 comments** (panelbear.com restatement). Commenters point back to McKinley’s original and earlier HN threads.  
4. **Earlier threads cited from that page:** [item 9291215](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=9291215) and [item 20323246](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=20323246).  
5. **[Choose Boring Technology](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46916487)** — boringtechnology.club; **19 points, 4 comments**. Hiring pool and “boring for *your* team” (e.g. sticking with Mongo if that is what you know).  
6. **[Choose Boring Technology, Revisited](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44739464)** — July 30, 2025; **7 points, 1 comment**. Short note that Django counts as boring now.  
7. **[The Boring Technology Manifesto](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47315575)** — author post describing a love letter to McKinley’s talk.  
8. **Related use of the idea:** [item 24432737](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=24432737) (innovation tokens vs. Phoenix/Elixir) and [item 16809127](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=16809127) (direct quote of the three-token passage).

A recent stub resubmission also indexes the big threads: [item 47872175](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47872175).

Interesting. Would you, when interviewing a 30-something fresh out of Etsy, assume they were unlikely to be a 'boring technology' advocate?
Because 'Choose Boring Technology' was originally an essay/talk given by Dan McKinley\[1\] describing the lessons he had learned at Etsy, which he left in 2014, approximately 12 years into his career. His strongest motivating example of a case where he 'chose boring technology' is a system his team built in 2010, when he would have been, I think, around 30. Is that 'a certain age'?

- [Anchises MoraestermOne of the founders of Garoa Hacker Clube, Brazil's first hackerspace, where he holds the ceremonial title of Supreme Chancellor; founder and organiser of Security BSides Sao Paulo; director of the Brazilian chapter of the Cloud Security Alliance; and author of the long-running blog AnchisesLandia.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/anchises-moraes/)
- [André-Marie AmpèreloreThe physicist who turned Ørsted's observation into electrodynamics, and who first drew the distinction between current and voltage.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/andre-marie-ampere/)
- [Android (as a Linux descendant)termThe most widely deployed Linux system in the world, and a deliberate piece of licence architecture: the copyleft kernel underneath, a permissively licensed framework and a purpose-built C library above it, so manufacturers can ship proprietary layers without publishing them.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/android-linux/)
- [anonymizationtermTransforming data so individuals can no longer be identified by any reasonably available means - the exit door from data protection law.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/anonymization/)
- [AnonymoustermThe leaderless online collective that emerged from imageboard culture around 2003 and became, from 2008, the public face of hacktivism - identified by the Guy Fawkes mask and the line 'We are Legion.' Anyone can act as Anonymous, which is the point and the problem.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/anonymous/)
- [ANPDacronymAutôridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados: Brazil's data protection authority - regulator, enforcer, and interpreter of the LGPD.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/anpd/)
- [anycasttermOne IP address announced from many locations, so users reach the nearest instance.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/anycast/)
- [Apache HTTP Server (httpd)termThe web server that ran most of the internet for the best part of two decades, begun in 1995 as coordinated patches to a server nobody was maintaining.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/apache-httpd/)
- [Apache Software Foundation (ASF)acronymThe non-profit incorporated in June 1999 so the Apache projects would outlive any individual volunteer.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/apache-software-foundation/)
- [APItermA defined way for one program to ask another for something - a contract about what may be called and what comes back.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/api/)
- [APIsec UniversitytermFree, certificate-granting API-security training - the fastest on-ramp into the OWASP API Top 10 world.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/apisec-university/)
- [App ConnectortermZPA's lightweight VM/container beside a private application, making only outbound TLS connections to Service Edges - enrolled with a provisioning key, discovering apps via its own DNS vantage.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/app-connector/)
- [App profile (ZCC)termThe Zscaler Client Connector policy object that decides per-application handling on the device: which destinations bypass the tunnel via its PAC logic, and platform-specific behavior per operating system.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/app-profile/)
- [AppleTalkloreApple's plug-and-play networking suite of the 1980s and 90s - zero-configuration before the term existed, now discontinued.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/appletalk/)
- [Application segmenttermZPA's unit of application definition: a set of FQDNs, wildcards, or IP addresses plus their ports, naming what can be reached. Access policy matches top-down against the most specific segment.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/app-segment/)
- [APT (Advanced Persistent Threat)acronymAn adversary with the resources and patience to gain access and keep it - typically state-sponsored or state-tolerated, focused on collection over months or years rather than on immediate gain. The term describes the operator's posture, not a specific technique.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/apt/)
- [ARC (Authenticated Received Chain)acronymA mechanism letting an intermediary - a forwarder or mailing list - record the authentication results it observed and sign that record, so a later receiver can tell that a message failed only because it was legitimately relayed.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/arc/)
- [archive formats (zip, tar, gz, 7z, rar, iso, cab)termContainer formats that bundle files together, compress them, or both - and the distinction between those two jobs is the thing most people never learn.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/archive-formats/)
- [Ariane 5 Flight 501loreThe 1996 maiden launch destroyed by an integer overflow in software reused from Ariane 4.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/ariane-5/)
- [ARPacronymAddress Resolution Protocol: how a host asks 'who has this IP?' on the local network and learns the answering MAC address.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/arp/)
- [ARP poisoningtermAnswering the local network's address resolution requests with a lie, so that traffic for another machine is delivered to you instead.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/arp-poisoning/)
- [ARPANETtermThe packet-switched network funded by ARPA that grew into the internet, beginning with four university nodes in 1969.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/arpanet/)
- [AS (autonomous system)acronymA network under one administrative routing policy, identified by an ASN.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/as/)
- [AS/400 (IBM i)termIBM's Application System/400, the midrange computer announced in June 1988 and released that August, whose operating system and architecture survive today as IBM i on Power Systems: a single-level store, an object-based machine interface and an integrated relational database that have kept forty-year-old applications running on current hardware.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/as-400/)
- [AS3acronymAn F5 extension for declaratively configuring application services via JSON.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/as3/)
- [ASCIIacronymThe 7-bit character code that numbers 0 to 127 the English letters, the digits, punctuation and 33 control codes; the first 128 code points of Unicode.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/ascii/)
- [ASICacronymApplication-Specific Integrated Circuit: a chip built to do one job, fast, and incapable of being repurposed.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/asic/)
- [ASLRacronymRandomizing where a process's memory regions land, so their addresses differ on every run.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/aslr/)
- [ASNacronymA number identifying a network under one routing policy.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/asn/)
- [assertiontermThe signed statement a federation protocol carries: who authenticated, when, how, for which audience, and for how long it is valid.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/assertion/)
- [assettermSomething an organisation owns or depends on that is worth protecting - and, in practice, something it has to know exists.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/asset/)
- [assume breachexpressionThe security posture that plans as if attackers are already inside, because someday they will be.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/assume-breach/)
- [asymmetric routingtermTraffic out one path and back another: perfectly legal IP behavior that quietly breaks stateful firewalls expecting to see both directions.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/asymmetric-routing/)
- [ATMacronymAsynchronous Transfer Mode - the 1990s bet that all traffic, voice to data, should ride fixed 53-byte cells with hard QoS. Ethernet and IP won instead.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/atm/)
- [ATP (Advanced Threat Protection)acronymA vendor product category - detonation sandboxes, mail and web filtering with behavioural analysis, endpoint detection bundled under one name - sold as the answer to advanced threats. Three letters away from APT, and constantly confused with it.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/atp/)
- [attack surfacetermEverything an attacker can reach and try: exposed services, APIs, credentials, people - the sum of ways in.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/attack-surface/)
- [attack vectortermThe specific path or means by which an attacker reaches and compromises a target.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/attack-vector/)
- [attackers only need to be right onceexpressionThe defender's dilemma: attackers can fail repeatedly at no cost, while defense must hold everywhere, always.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/attackers-only-need-to-be-right-once/)
- [attenuationtermSignal loss over distance and through obstacles, measured in dB - the budget every link spends whether copper, fiber, or radio.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/attenuation/)
- [attestationtermA statement by one party that something about another is true, made in a form somebody else is willing to rely on.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/attestation/)
- [Atwood's lawexpression'Any application that can be written in JavaScript, will eventually be written in JavaScript.'](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/atwoods-law/)
- [audittermAn independent examination of whether controls exist and operate as described, producing an opinion somebody else can rely on.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/audit/)
- [audit trailtermThe tamper-evident record of who did what, when, and from where - the API log every investigation starts from.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/audit-trail/)
- [authenticationtermEstablishing who or what is making a request - distinct from deciding what they may do.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/authentication/)
- [authentication adaptertermThe PingFederate component that actually authenticates a user - or receives one authenticated elsewhere: HTML Form, HTTP Basic, Kerberos, OpenToken, and Reference ID each embody a different integration pattern.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/authentication-adapter/)
- [Authentication Policy ContracttermThe normalized attribute set an authentication policy fulfills on every successful path: whatever adapter or IdP connection authenticated the user, downstream configuration consumes the same contract.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/authentication-policy-contract/)
- [authentication policy treetermPingFederate's runtime decision tree for authentication: nodes are authentication sources and selectors, Fail and Success branches express fallbacks, reusable fragments capture common sequences, and every successful path ends by fulfilling a policy contract.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/authentication-policy-tree/)
- [authorizationtermDeciding what an authenticated party may do - the check that runs on every request, not just at the door.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/authorization/)
- [auto-negotiationtermThe exchange in which two twisted-pair Ethernet ports advertise their speeds and duplex modes and settle on the best they share.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/auto-negotiation/)
- [autoscalingtermCapacity that follows demand: instances added on load, removed in quiet - elasticity as the cloud's founding promise.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/autoscaling/)
- [availability zonetermOne or more data centers with independent power, cooling, and network inside a region - close enough for sync replication, far enough to fail separately.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/availability-zone/)
- [AWSacronymAmazon's cloud platform - compute, storage, networking, and hundreds of services.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/aws/)

## B81

- [Babel FishloreThe web's first machine-translation service, shipped by AltaVista.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/babel-fish/)
- [baby giantjargonA frame just slightly over the classic 1518-byte Ethernet maximum - grown by tags and labels, not by payload.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/baby-giant/)
- [Back OrificeloreThe remote-administration tool for Windows released by the Cult of the Dead Cow at DEF CON in August 1998, its name a joke at the expense of Microsoft's BackOffice. It gave an operator near-total control of a remote Windows machine over a small, quiet network channel.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/back-orifice/)
- [backhaultermThe links carrying aggregated access traffic from towers, cabinets, and OLTs back to the network core - the middle mile.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/backhaul/)
- [backhoe fadejargonTelecom's dry name for total signal loss caused by construction equipment digging through the fiber.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/backhoe-fade/)
- [backuptermA copy kept so that data can be recovered - which is only true once a restore has been tested.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/backup/)
- [backup vs. snapshotexpressionSnapshots are fast local restore points sharing the original's fate; backups live elsewhere and survive it - only the second answers ransomware.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/shadow-copy/)
- [BADoSacronymA defense that detects denial-of-service by learning normal traffic behavior.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/bados/)
- [Banking trojantermMalware built specifically to steal money from online banking sessions - by capturing credentials, injecting fake fields into the bank's page, drawing a convincing overlay window on top of the real application, or altering payment details as a transfer is submitted.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/banking-trojan/)
- [Barbara LiskovloreThe 2008 Turing Award recipient, cited for practical and theoretical foundations of programming language and system design, especially data abstraction, fault tolerance and distributed computing.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/barbara-liskov/)
- [Barnaby JackloreThe New Zealand researcher whose 2010 Black Hat talk 'Jackpotting Automated Teller Machines' made two ATMs spray cash across the stage on command - the single most-cited demonstration in conference history, and the origin of jackpotting as a term.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/barnaby-jack/)
- [Base64termAn encoding that represents arbitrary bytes using 64 printable characters, so binary data can travel through channels that only accept text.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/base64/)
- [bastion hosttermThe one hardened, audited entry point for administrative access to a private network - a jump host by design rather than accident.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/bastion-host/)
- [bazloreThe third metasyntactic placeholder, following foo and bar.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/baz/)
- [BCP 38 (source address validation)termThe practice of a network verifying that packets leaving it carry source addresses that actually belong to it, and dropping those that do not - blocking address forgery at the point where it originates.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/bcp38/)
- [beaconingjargonThe regular, automated check-ins a compromised host makes to its command server.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/beaconing/)
- [BEASTloreA 2011 attack decrypting TLS 1.0 traffic by exploiting predictable CBC initialization vectors.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/beast/)
- [BEBacronymAn edge device in an Ethernet fabric that encapsulates traffic into the backbone.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/beb/)
- [belt and suspendersexpressionWearing two independent safeguards for the same failure - if one lets go, the trousers stay up.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/belt-and-suspenders/)
- [BFDacronymBidirectional Forwarding Detection - a tiny, protocol-agnostic hello stream that detects a dead path in milliseconds, so routing protocols can fail over before users notice.](https://ronutz.com/de/glossary/bfd/)
